observation: PepsiCo printed a 52-week low with revenue growth 5.6 percent and roughly 17x trailing earnings; McDonald's 6.3 percent and 20x. Multiple compression with fundamentals intact is what a discount-rate channel looks like.
XLU hit a 52-week low while AI represents the largest new source of electricity demand in forty years. Only a rate channel reconciles those two facts.
A large share of the new-low list is consumer rather than bond proxy: McDonald's, Nike, Lowe's, AutoZone. The K-shaped consumer thesis explains those without any rate channel.
One-month rolling correlation between front-month WTI and the 10-year yield reached 0.96, the tightest since 2019. A single factor is driving the cross-section to both tails.
Refiners Marathon Petroleum and Valero appear on the 7-name new-high list while fuel-consuming and low-income-exposed names dominate the 30-name new-low list.
AMD and Warner Bros Discovery are on the new-high list for reasons unrelated to crude: an AI chip rally and a merger settlement. The high list is at least three unrelated buckets, not one.
Magnificent 7 CY2026 consensus EPS growth 22.8 percent against 12.1 percent for the other 493. Tech sector EPS growth 32 percent against 7.7 for utilities.
NVIDIA alone accounts for roughly 65 percent of the Magnificent 7 growth rate. Ex-NVIDIA the group grows 14.8 percent against 12.1 for the 493, a gap too narrow to carry the concentration argument.
Alphabet turned free-cash-flow negative in Q2 2026 for the first time while long-term debt more than doubled to 98bn over the first half.

S&P states hyperscaler credit quality is gradually weakening, with financings becoming more complicated and less transparent. Moody's counts roughly 662bn of signed but not commenced data-centre leases held off balance sheet.
Nike was removed from the S&P 100 on 21 September, the same session it printed a new 52-week low. Index deletions force mechanical selling into weakness.
Index weights did not change materially during Q3, yet the breadth split is only about one quarter old. A slow structural feature cannot explain a fast change.
US restaurant traffic was negative in six of seven months in 2026 while retail visits stayed positive. Grocers, mass merchants and clubs gained as consumers traded down.
McDonald's has described low-income QSR traffic falling nearly double digits for roughly two years while higher-income traffic rose nearly double digits.

Equal-weight S&P returned 12.1 percent in H1 2026 against 10.2 percent cap-weighted, so the narrowing is roughly one quarter old and began when oil and yields spiked. This dates the regime and argues against a multi-year mania framing.
